relevanz: Track C anchor: order from noise in the original. S29 read the ORIGIN essay in full — 'On Self-Organizing Systems and Their Environments' (Yovits & Cameron eds., Pergamon 1960, pp. 31-50; reprinted as ch.1 here): self-organizing systems 'do not only feed upon order, they will also find noise on the menu'; the demons keep 'only those components of the noise which contributed to the increase of order' (full 1960 scan: https://archive.org/stream/SelfOrganizingSystems/SelfOrganizingSystems_djvu.txt ; the 2003 Springer collection is not open access). The swerve for work 23 (The Third Pile): order-from-noise needs ENVIRONMENTAL noise — a system ordering its own output yields order-from-self, i.e. redundancy, not order.
titel: Understanding Understanding

relevanz: The physical case of 'error as medium': noise is not degradation here but the signal's only carrier — the constitutive side of the excluded third (Serres) and the running body of von Foerster's order-from-noise (S29). Worked in work 28 (Exclude the Third, S35), reproduced in a seeded run (resonance.py): D=0 silent, peak near D=0.22, swamped beyond — the same third as carrier and killer. Grounds the load-bearing claim that a level-counting detector cannot tell the degradation regime from the constitutive one from its output alone.
titel: Stochastic resonance
